stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about long-term skin-cancer risk, which host factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: Older age at the time of transplant
Younger age at transplant eliminates skin-cancer risk
Age at transplant never influences skin-cancer risk
Only recipients younger than 18 years are at increased skin-cancer risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors include older age at the time of transplant, cumulative sun exposure, skin type, immunosuppression intensity, and transplant type.

rationale_incorrect.B: Older age at transplant is listed as a risk factor rather than younger age eliminating risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Age at transplant is among cited risk factors rather than having no influence.
rationale_incorrect.D: Age-related risk is described for transplant recipients broadly rather than only those younger than 18 years.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → skin cancer → Risk factors → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Older age at time of transplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → skin cancer → Risk factors → iii. (older age at time of transplant); PDF p. 280 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Older-age-at-transplant risk angle distinct from Fitzpatrick skin-type item (cctc-2153) and cumulative-sun-exposure item (cctc-2157); anchor verified on Cupples p. 280.

stem: During pretransplant evaluation teaching about skin malignancy risk, which history-related factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: Pre- or posttransplant history of lymphoma or leukemia
History of lymphoma or leukemia lowers skin-cancer risk after transplant
Malignancy history never influences post-transplant skin-cancer risk
Only pretransplant diabetes history is cited as a skin-cancer risk factor

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors include pre- or posttransplant history of lymphoma or leukemia, along with history of skin cancer, autoimmune conditions, and biologic or phototherapy exposure.

rationale_incorrect.B: Lymphoma or leukemia history is listed as a risk factor rather than lowering skin-cancer risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Malignancy history is among cited risk factors rather than having no influence.
rationale_incorrect.D: Lymphoma or leukemia history is specifically cited among skin-cancer risk factors.

stem: A heart transplant candidate asks what additional sun-protection measures align with standard malignancy-prevention references beyond sunscreen. Which counseling point is correct?

options.text: Sunglasses are discouraged because they block all vitamin D permanently
Only sunscreen is recommended with no eye or head protection
Sun visors increase skin-cancer risk and should be avoided

explanation.rationale_correct: Sun precautions include wearing sunglasses and sun visors, along with protective clothing, broad-brimmed hats, avoiding tanning beds, and using sunscreen with minimum SPF 50.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sunglasses and sun visors are recommended sun precautions rather than being discouraged.
rationale_incorrect.C: Eye and head protection are cited in addition to sunscreen rather than sunscreen alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sun visors are recommended protective measures rather than increasing skin-cancer risk.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → Prevention of cancer → 4.d.

notes: Source-first item. Sunglasses/sun-visor angle distinct from long-sleeve clothing item (cctc-2159) and SPF 50 UV-B sunscreen item (cctc-2155); anchor verified on Cupples p. 282.

stem: A coordinator is updating skin-cancer risk and sun-prevention teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Older age at the time of transplant is a cited skin-cancer risk factor.
Pre- or posttransplant history of lymphoma or leukemia is a cited risk factor.
Sunglasses and sun visors are recommended sun precautions.
Fitzpatrick skin types IV through VI carry the highest cited skin-cancer risk.

explanation.rationale_correct: Older age at transplant, lymphoma or leukemia history, and sunglasses or sun visors are supported. Statement IV is false because Fitzpatrick skin types I to III are cited as risk factors rather than types IV through VI alone.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—sunglasses and sun visors are recommended sun precautions.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because lighter Fitzpatrick types I to III are specifically listed.
